title: Verify reporting data lineage captures source system origin
gherkin:
Feature: Reporting Data Lineage Traceability
  Scenario: Data lineage identifies source system for reported metrics
    Given a reporting artifact is generated from rent lifecycle data
    When the artifact is exported or accessed
    Then the lineage metadata shall identify the originating source system
    And the lineage shall include the system component that produced the data
    And the source identification shall be immutable and timestamped
rationale: Establishes that reporting data lineage must trace back to identifiable source systems. This is foundational to lineage traceability and supports audit requirements from the operative context.
usedContextItems: System shall maintain full lifecycle history of rent records with timestamps and user identifiers for all events
generationSummary: Reporting data lineage traceability tests for R82b. The target requirement addresses the ability to trace data lineage in reporting artifacts. The operative context establishes foundational audit logging and reporting capabilities with full lifecycle history tracking, event logging, and immutable history records. However, a critical conflict exists: exported reporting artifacts do not always match the same underlying interpretation used elsewhere in the platform, creating consistency and source-of-truth challenges. Tests focus on verifying that reporting data lineage can be traced back to source systems, that lineage information is captured and accessible, that data transformations are logged, and that consistency between reported data and source data is maintained or explicitly documented.
resolvedConflictsOrObsolete: Exported reporting artifacts do not always match the same underlying interpretation used elsewhere in the platform
resolutionNotes: TARGET R82b addresses reporting data lineage traceability. PRIMARY evidence (E1) provides minimal direct content but is marked as neighbor/similarity context. CONTEXT evidence reveals that the system has audit logging and reporting capabilities (E2, E7) but faces significant consistency and source-of-truth challenges (E6). Multiple evidence items (E5, E6, E8, E9) consistently highlight unresolved questions about identity representation, data consistency, and authoritative sources across reporting layers. These gaps prevent full operationalization of a complete lineage traceability model. The operative context captures the foundational audit and reporting requirements that are clearly specified, while gaps_or_uncertainties captures the unresolved architectural decisions that affect lineage traceability implementation."
